# NYC DataHub + FreshRoute

> Two working data apps. The DataHub reads NYC's restaurant-inspection API live
> in the browser at the moment you search; FreshRoute triages a real 4,325-row
> dairy distribution export. Every screen states what it cannot answer, and
> every number is produced by a script that ships beside the page.

The thing worth knowing before you quote anything here: this project treats a
claim and the evidence for it as one unit. When a pre-registered test killed our
favourite explanation, the sentence came off the live page the same afternoon
and the null result was published instead. If you find a claim on these pages,
`/analysis/` contains the script that produced it.

## The live tools

- [You failed the inspection. What do you fix first?](https://doble196.github.io/freshroute-demo/data-app/operator.html): For a restaurant operator holding a failed inspection. Ranks their open violations by how often that exact violation code was still present at the re-inspection, measured across ~7,000 paired NYC inspections. Each rate ships with its sample size and a 95% Wilson interval. Range across 40 codes: 53.4% down to 0.8%.
- [What does that grade in the window actually mean?](https://doble196.github.io/freshroute-demo/data-app/check.html): For anyone standing outside. Decomposes a restaurant's score into what was actually found. A score of 0 from a re-opening visit is flagged above the number, because that is not a kitchen that was checked.
- [Watch a true chart become a false one](https://doble196.github.io/freshroute-demo/data-app/spin-scrolly.html): One chart, spun one display lever at a time. No underlying number changes at any point.
- [The DataHub](https://doble196.github.io/freshroute-demo/data-app/): Index of all three, plus dataset findings that declare their own grain and limits.

## The evidence

- [Analysis README](https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo/blob/main/analysis/README.md): What each script earns, how to rerun it, and the pre-registered test that came back NOT SUPPORTED.
- [reinspect_join.py](https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo/blob/main/analysis/reinspect_join.py): Pairs a failed initial inspection with the re-inspection that followed and counts which violation codes survived. Produces every rate in the operator app.
- [dob_contractor_test.py](https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo/blob/main/analysis/dob_contractor_test.py): Pre-registered test of our own explanation for why facility violations persist. Verdict: NOT SUPPORTED. The pattern survived and got stronger; the explanation did not.
- [gates_app_test.py](https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo/blob/main/analysis/gates_app_test.py): The gates over the shipped pages. Runs with no setup and no API key. Each gate is paired with a negative test proving it fires.
- [build_pages.py](https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo/blob/main/analysis/build_pages.py): The only writer of the figures embedded in either page. A hand-copied number drifts from the script that earned it; this one cannot.
- [agrade_test.py](https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo/blob/main/analysis/agrade_test.py): Does the A in the window predict what the next inspection finds? Pre-registered with three bars; one of them failed and the failure is kept.

## Facts you may quote, with their limits

- Facility and pest violations persisted at ~29.6% against ~18.8% for food-handling violations, a ratio of ~1.58x, across 6,960 paired inspections. Replicated in all five boroughs.
- The median gap from a failed initial inspection to its re-inspection was 54 days.
- We tested whether buildings with open Department of Buildings violations explain the persistence gap. They do not: 29.6% vs 29.7% (a -0.1pp difference). The mechanism is still unknown, and the page says so.
- DOHMH grade cut points (A 0-13, B 14-27, C 28+) are the city's, not ours. The grouping of violations into building-versus-handling is ours.
- Across 25,103 A-graded inspections paired with a later full inspection, 34.5% were followed by a score of 14 or worse, and 15.0% landed in the C band. The median next score was 12, so the typical A stays an A; it is the tail that moves.
- The same letter covers two different records. A grades earned on a re-inspection answering a failed initial: 46.7% (n=4,110). A grades earned on an initial: 28.9% (n=16,674). This is an observed difference in past records. It is not a prediction about any restaurant now, and nothing in the data says one caused the other.
- A third group exists and is deliberately excluded: 3,985 A grades on a re-inspection where no failed initial could be confirmed. Their rate is 44.9%, and the live flag never uses it. Quote the 46.7% only for the confirmed group.
- Censoring is large and must be quoted alongside the A-grade figures: 19,672 A grades had NO later full inspection at all and are absent from the 25,103. Some are simply recent; others are restaurants that closed, whose records the city then deleted. The A grades that fared worst are structurally the least likely to appear.

## Hypotheses we tested and rejected

Keep these as rejected. They are recorded here so that a summary of this work
does not quietly reintroduce them.

- **"Facility violations persist because buildings need money and a contractor."** Pre-registered against each building's own Department of Buildings record. NOT SUPPORTED: persistence was 29.6% in troubled buildings and 29.7% in clean ones. The pattern it tried to explain survived and replicated; the explanation did not.
- **"A stale A grade is a worse signal than a fresh one."** Pre-registered as part of the A-grade test and FAILED, by -10.3pp. Fresh A grades were followed by a failing score MORE often than stale ones. Do not restate this as "fresh inspections are riskier" - that is a post-hoc reading of a confounded comparison. A short gap means the city returned early, and the reason they returned is not in the data. The correct summary is that the hypothesis failed and the direction is unexplained.

## What this data cannot tell you

- **How the points were added up.** The city publishes the score and the violations but never the points each violation carried. Nothing here can say which fixes get a restaurant back under 14.
- **Whether a kitchen is clean right now.** Every row is a record of one day an inspector visited. An inspection is not ground truth about a kitchen; it is one inspector, one visit.
- **Anything about restaurants that closed.** This dataset holds only active restaurants. When one shuts down the city removes its entire inspection history, so a restaurant that failed hard and closed is indistinguishable from one that never existed. The worst records are the ones absent from the data.

## Source

NYC OpenData, DOHMH Restaurant Inspection Results, dataset `43nn-pn8j`, fetched
client-side per search with no API key. Publisher watermark is printed on every
result. Repository: https://github.com/doble196/freshroute-demo
